newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end mixed despite New York's plunge.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end mixed despite New York's plunge.

text.p: Toronto's stock market ended mixed on Wednesday as downward pressure from a tumbling Wall Street offset surging golds.
The exchange's key 300 Composite Index dipped 8.44 points to close at 6121.52. The Dow Jones Industrial Average shed 140 points to hit 7085.65 after Tuesday's new high of 7300.
Trading was active at 123.3 million shares worth C$1.5 billion ($1.1 billion).
Canada's largest equities market was buoyed by a soaring gold sector, which gained almost 3.3 percent.
"That was a nice bounce in the golds," said Pier Donnini, head trader of institutional equities at Yorkton Securities. "That basically saved our bacon."
In New York, "basically everybody was in the mood to take profits and when it started down, people got nervous," said Michael Metz, investment advisor at Oppenheimer & Co Inc.

Metz said the nervousness began with the morning's U.S. economic data. First-quarter U.S. business productivity outside the farm sector rise 2.0 percent on an annualized basis, short of the 2.4 percent gain expected by economists. But March wholesale investories rose 0.7 percent compared to forecasts of 0.4 percent.
Analysts said a disappointing 10-year $12 billion bond auction in the United States then sparked the sell-off in North American bond markets and on Wall Street.
Of Toronto's 14 sub-indices, only golds and conglomerates rose while the rest fell, led by consumer products, transportation and media.
The broader market was mixed, with advancing issues outnumbering decliners 494 to 469, while 313 traded flat.
In individual issues, closely watched Bre-X Minerals Ltd. inched up half a cent to 0.09 on more than 20 million shares on its last day of trading in Toronto.
After the session's close, the Toronto Stock Exchange delisted Bre-X following its roller-coaster ride from pennies to a high of 28.65 after a 10-for-1 stock split to pennies again.
A report on Sunday declared Bre-X's Indonesian gold find a fraud, dashing investor hopes for a deposit once touted as the world's largest.
